quizName: Hardest Questions in Utah Most difficult questions from your region.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: A baseball cap that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a jacket and long pants made of strong material, boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT protective clothing for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing: sturdy pants and jackets that cover your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover and support your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: For the best protection, wear a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets DOT and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no obvious defects.

questions.question: Use a turn signal:

options.text: When you plan to speed up
Only when there is heavy traffic

questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Which of the following should you check before riding?

options.text: The amount of cushion on your seat

questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, tail light, turn signals, brake light, clutch and throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of an accident, you should:

options.text: Blend into traffic so other drivers don't notice you
Not use turn signals unless riding at night
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning
Ride very close to the vehicle ahead of you

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and turning
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers. Use your turn signals, brake light, and proper lane position. Keep space between you and other vehicles, look 12 seconds ahead, and be ready to react to hazards.

questions.question: Space between your motorcycle and other vehicles:

options.text: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake
Limits your movement in your lane
Lets you rely on others to spot hazards
Requires you to drive faster to keep up

questions.correctAnswerText: Gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast:

options.text: Can cause you to drift into another lane
Is better than going too slowly
Usually keeps you in your lane
Is okay because motorcycles are small

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to drift into another lane
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before you turn.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can be more visible by:

options.text: Riding very close to other vehicles

questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: Checking your mirrors:

options.text: Should be part of your regular scanning routine
Should be avoided because they distract you
Should be avoided because other drivers see you easily
Is only recommended in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your regular scanning routine
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often so you know what is behind you. Mirror checks should be part of your normal routine.

questions.question: For the best protection, make sure your helmet:
questions.explanation: Buy a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly around your head and have no visible damage.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone who owns a different type of motorcycle.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed bike. It teaches you about your specific motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, clothing:

options.text: Should be loose enough to flap in the wind.
Should not fully cover your arms or legs.
Should not include a jacket in warm weather.
Can protect you if you crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect you if you crash.
questions.explanation: Good clothing protects you in a crash. Always wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs, even on warm days. Your clothes should fit snugly so they don't flap but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries are reduced by:
questions.explanation: A good helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in an accident.

questions.question: When using an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Test the seat to make sure it is comfortable.
Assume the motorcycle is in good condition.
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
Ride as you normally do because most bikes are similar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding.
questions.explanation: Each motorcycle is different, so be careful with a new one. Learn how it works before you ride. Practice using the throttle, clutch, and brakes several times to get familiar with them.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are often:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: When checking tire pressure:

options.text: Looking at the tire is a good method.
Squeeze the tire to check it.
Compare your tire height to another tire.

questions.explanation: Use a tire gauge to check your tire pressure before every ride. You cannot judge pressure by looking at the tire because it may look fine even when it is under-inflated.

questions.question: Which color helps you be seen while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green when riding. Bright clothing makes you easier for others to see, no matter what time of day you ride.

questions.question: Even if your turn is obvious, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need a signal if pedestrians are nearby.
Only need a signal at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes, even if it seems obvious. Other vehicles nearby may not see you. There could be vehicles you haven't noticed.

questions.question: For maximum protection, wear a helmet certified by the:
questions.explanation: Use a motorcycle helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards for maximum protection.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders should wear shoes with soles that:
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are high and sturdy to support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: For the best protection, choose a helmet that:

options.text: Has been in a crash before.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Work as well as a face shield.
Protect as much as a windshield.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only, not your whole face. A face shield is better because it protects your entire face. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, the laces should:
questions.explanation: Tuck in your laces securely so they do not catch on your motorcycle.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other riders and be seen by them. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you a way to escape if danger appears.
